A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IIS/IISA task, IISA-DB dataset and WIISA method. Their complete main texts and supplementary material, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original subjective annotations, dataset reliability analyses, predictive experiments and ablations, including Tables 1–3 and S1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original subjective-study outcomes, reliability analyses and model experiments reported in Tables 1–3 and S1.

M1.justification: WIISA retains the same scale sampling, Lanczos downscaling, piecewise weak-label rule and training-batch augmentation. The annotation aggregation, predictive models and inference procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 785-image IISA-DB, comprising 248 KonIQ-10k and 537 Pixabay images, and the same additional datasets for pretraining and analysis. The applications and future image types discussed in v2 are not newly evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains DBCNN, TOPIQ, CONTRIQUE, ARNIQA, CLIP-IQA+ and QualiCLIP with the same Base/WIISA comparisons. Tables 1 and S1 retain the same SPAQ- and UHD-IQA-pretrained TOPIQ variants.

E3.justification: Section 6.3 removes the reported procedure that partitions KonX images by the resolution maximizing MOS and averages scores within those groups. The retained prediction experiments keep the same 70/10/20 splits, metrics, preprocessing and testing procedures.

E4.justification: v2 removes the grouped KonX analysis supporting the assumed quality–scale relationship, previously shown in Figure 6. The individual-image consistency check, supplementary resampling analysis, Table 3 ablations and other supplementary analyses remain.

E5.justification: The 100-resample confidence-interval analysis moves from v1 Section S2.5 to v2 Section 4.2, retaining the same procedure and reported intervals. Ten cross-validation repetitions, median test reporting, inter-group uncertainty reporting and Section S1.3 resampling are unchanged.

E6.justification: The three grouped KonX quality trajectories and their average-level finding in v1 Figure 6 are absent from v2. All methods, rows and numerical values in Tables 1–3 and S1 match exactly; the 378/420 (90%) individual-image consistency result also remains.

T1.justification: Equations (1), (2) and (S1), the monotonicity assumptions and their mathematical reasoning are unchanged. The added latent-expectation discussion clarifies the interpretation of subjective measurements without revising the formal definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same IIS definition, IISA task, expert-annotated dataset, WIISA contribution and consistent-improvement claim. Added emphasis on verified reliability restates a claim already made in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes latent perceptual values from noisy observed averages and adds a viewing-distance/resolution equivalence rationale in Section 6.3. Sections S1.4 and S5 expand application interpretations and future validation needs; the existing annotation-cost and interpolation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section S3.1 retains the same 1536-pixel crops, flip probability, weak-label settings and H100 80GB hardware disclosure. Data-curation and annotation instructions remain equivalent, and both versions promise code, data and pretrained models upon acceptance.

R1.justification: Huang et al.'s High Resolution Image Quality Database, reference 16 in v1, disappears from v2's bibliography, leaving an unresolved citation beside KonX in Section S3.2. The remaining related-work coverage and novelty positioning are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory prose and applications/future-work subsections, moves applications from the introduction to Section 3, and brings appendix reliability and viewing-condition discussions into Section 4.2. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 6 is removed, while the image-width distribution moves from Figure 3 to supplementary Figure S4. Other graphics are retained with renumbering or repositioning; Table 2 relocates and Figure 1's caption expands. The retained graphic contents and table structures match.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies latent perceptual quantities and makes existing annotation-reliability evidence easier to assess in Section 4.2. These limited clarity gains are partly offset by the removed grouped KonX visualization and unresolved citation in Section S3.2. The main predictive evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
